_meta.indication: Long-term enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for adults with a confirmed diagnosis of Type 1 Gaucher disease.

pivotal_trials.design: 9-month, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial comparing two doses (30 Units/kg vs 60 Units/kg every other week).
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve patients with Type 1 Gaucher disease requiring splenomegaly (>8 times normal by MRI) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count <120,000/mm3).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in mean spleen volume (primary efficacy endpoint) after nine months.
pivotal_trials.n: 32 treatment-naïve patients randomized; 31 evaluable for efficacy (15 at 30 Units/kg, 16 at 60 Units/kg).
pivotal_trials.result: After nine months, mean spleen volume decreased 29% in the 30 Units/kg group and 40% in the 60 Units/kg group. In a gender subgroup analysis of percentage change from baseline in spleen volume, the within-subgroup one-sample t-test p-values were significant in both female (p=0.0001 and p<0.0001) and male (p=0.0004 and p<0.0001) patients.

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase III Trial to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Plant Cell Expressed GCD in Patients With Gaucher Disease

key_safety: Infusion reactions (including allergic reactions) within 24 hours were the most common reactions (44%-46% of patients); anaphylaxis occurred in 9% (3/32) of treatment-naïve patients in PB-06-001. Other commonly observed adverse reactions (≥10% of patients) included URTI/nasopharyngitis (22%/18%), pharyngitis/throat infection (19%/4%), headache (19%/11%), and arthralgia (13%/11%).
target_moa: Taliglucerase alfa is a hydrolytic lysosomal glucocerebroside-specific enzyme (recombinant human glucocerebrosidase) that compensates for the enzymatic deficiency underlying Gaucher disease, reducing accumulation of glucocerebroside within macrophages.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human glucocerebrosidase expressed in carrot plant root cells).

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was held due to the product's similarity to other approved enzyme replacement therapies for Type 1 Gaucher disease.

summary.text: Taliglucerase alfa received Fast Track designation (August 24, 2009) and orphan designation (September 3, 2009) for Type 1 Gaucher disease. The NDA was submitted April 26, 2010 with standard review; a Complete Response letter issued February 24, 2011 was followed by a complete response submitted August 1, 2011, leading to approval of this standard (non-accelerated) application.
